directions: Start indoors or direct sow in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Prizm is an All-America Selections-winning kale bred for a compact, dense, more uniform habit than older kale varieties, with tender, tightly curled, blue-green leaves that hold good quality and mild flavor even as the plant matures. Its smaller stature makes it well suited to containers and smaller garden beds, and the tender texture requires less cooking time than some older, tougher kale cultivars, making it popular for salads as well as cooked greens. Harvest outer leaves regularly to encourage continued production, and like other kale, flavor sweetens after light frost in a fall crop.

common_name: Darkibor Kale (Dark Blue-Green Curly Hybrid Kale)

planting.note: Start indoors or direct sow; kale is also an excellent fall crop, since cool weather and light frost sweeten the leaves' flavor.

directions: Start indoors or direct sow in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Darkibor is a vigorous hybrid curly kale producing densely ruffled, dark blue-green leaves on a productive, uniform plant, valued commercially and by home gardeners alike for reliable yields and good cold tolerance that lets it stand in the garden well into winter in many climates. The tightly curled leaf texture holds up well to cooking methods like sauteing and braising, and the dark color signals a good concentration of nutrients typical of kale. Harvest outer leaves as needed, working from the bottom up, and expect improved sweetness after the plant experiences a light frost.

planting.note: Start indoors or direct sow; kale is also an excellent fall crop, since cool weather and light frost sweeten the leaves' flavor.

directions: Start indoors or direct sow in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Darto is a striking Lacinato-type (dinosaur kale) selection with unusually dark, almost blue-black, deeply savoyed leaves, even darker than standard Lacinato kale, giving it strong ornamental value in addition to its classic sweet, nutty flavor prized in Tuscan cooking. The long, narrow, crinkled leaves hold their quality well in cool weather and are excellent massaged raw into salads, sauteed, or added to soups. Harvest outer leaves as needed, allowing the central growing point to continue producing new leaves over a long season, and expect the flavor to sweeten further after light frost.

common_name: Westland Winter Kale (Classic Hardy British Curly Kale)

planting.note: Start indoors or direct sow; kale is also an excellent fall crop, since cool weather and light frost sweeten the leaves' flavor.

directions: Start indoors or direct sow in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Westland Winter is a classic, cold-hardy curly kale long grown in Britain for reliable winter harvests, producing dense, tightly ruffled, blue-green leaves on sturdy, productive plants that stand up well to cold, wind, and less-than-ideal soil. Its exceptional cold hardiness makes it a strong choice for extending the harvest deep into winter in colder climates, and like other kale it becomes noticeably sweeter and more tender after exposure to frost. Harvest outer leaves regularly from the bottom of the plant upward, leaving the central rosette to continue producing new growth over the season.
